# 116 — Dependency_Resolved

Indicates that the requested application component was supplied successfully\.

[All events](index.md) · [Dependency category](Category_Dependency.md) · [API reference](xref:Patware.Diagnostics.ApplicationEvents.DependencyEvents.Resolved%28System.String%2CSystem.String%2CSystem.String%29)

| Field | Value |

| EventId | 116 |

| Category | [Dependency](Category_Dependency.md) |
| Event class | LowLevel |

| Status | Stable |
| Introduced | 0.0.10 |

## Usage

Import `Patware.Diagnostics.ApplicationEvents`. This example assumes an existing
`ILogger` named `logger` and caller-supplied variables for the arguments.

```csharp
logger.Dependency.Resolved(@dependencyName, @operationName, @resolutionId);
```

**Trigger:** Emit immediately after obtaining the required component, before performing business operations with it\.

**Message template:** Dependency \{DependencyName\} resolved\. Operation: \{OperationName\}\. Resolution: \{ResolutionId\}\.

## Arguments

- `dependencyName` (`string`): The logical component name used by the beginning event\.
- `operationName` (`string`): The logical operation name used by the beginning event\.
- `resolutionId` (`string`): The identifier of the successfully completed resolution attempt\.

## Remarks

- Use the same dependency name, operation name, and resolution identifier as Dependency\_Resolving\.
- A cached instance satisfies resolution; this event does not imply that a new instance was constructed\.
- A null result from an optional lookup does not establish that the requested component was supplied\.
- Successful resolution does not prove external connectivity, business\-operation success, component health, or initialization of every application dependency\.
- This event does not indicate recovery from degraded application mode\.
- Calling this method only emits a diagnostic record\. It does not resolve components or change application state\.
